title: The store branch cannot be deleted or rewritten
context: The blueprint-changes branch is the durable store of every Change page, and ADR-0075's freeze check reads the G1 version of a Proposal from its history. No ruleset covered it, so it could be deleted or force-pushed, and its earliest commit is already later than a measurement taken of it days before, so its history has been rebuilt once.
decision: A GitHub ruleset forbids deleting blueprint-changes and pushing to it anything but a fast-forward. The store shrinks, when it has to, only through ordinary commits or by moving pages to another ref, never by rewriting its history.

alternatives.option: Leave the branch unprotected and rely on publish never forcing a push
alternatives.reason: Publish never forces, but a person or a one-off conversion script can, and one already rebuilt the history; the freeze check silently loses the version it compares against.

consequences: Converting every page to a new format (ADR-0079) is done with ordinary commits on top of the store, never by rebuilding the branch.
Rewriting the store's history requires lifting the ruleset first, as an explicit decision.
revisitTriggers: The store's history has to be rewritten, for example to drop pages that must not be kept, which requires lifting the ruleset as an explicit decision.
